title: VT S0023: An act relating to the use of synthetic media in elections

obligations: A person shall not, within 90 days before an election in Vermont, publish, communicate, or otherwise distribute synthetic media that the person knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media unless the person includes a disclosure stating: "This media has been manipulated or generated by digital technology and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur." (§ 2032(a))

For images and video recordings, the disclosure text must be easily readable by the average viewer and inclusive to the greatest extent possible of individuals with disabilities, and for video recordings, the disclosure must appear for the full duration (§ 2032(a)(1)).

For audio recordings only, the disclosure must be read in a clearly spoken manner and in a pitch and pace that can be easily heard by the average listener and inclusive to the greatest extent possible of individuals with disabilities, at the beginning, at the end, and if longer than two minutes, interspersed at intervals not greater than two minutes each (§ 2032(a)(2)).
A person upon whom a notice is served under civil investigation must comply with its terms unless otherwise ordered by a court (§ 2042(b)(1)).
prohibitions: Publishing, communicating, or otherwise distributing synthetic media that the person knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media within 90 days before an election in Vermont without the required disclosure (§ 2032(a)).
Knowingly and intentionally violating any provision of this subchapter (§ 2033(a)).
With intent to avoid, evade, or prevent compliance with a civil investigation, removing, concealing, withholding, destroying, mutilating, altering, or falsifying documentary material (§ 2042(b)(2)).

Passed 2026-03-10. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This act requires a disclosure on synthetic media that is deceptive and fraudulent when published, communicated, or distributed within 90 days before an election in Vermont. It sets specific format requirements for the disclosure in images, video, and audio, and provides penalties for knowing and intentional violations. It also gives enforcement and investigation powers to the Attorney General and State's Attorneys, and allows candidates to seek injunctive relief.

Who it applies to

  • Any person who publishes, communicates, or otherwise distributes synthetic media within 90 days before an election in Vermont (§ 2032(a))
  • Candidates whose appearance, speech, conduct, or environment is misrepresented through deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media (§ 2033(b))
  • State's Attorney and Attorney General for enforcement and investigation (§ 2041, § 2042)

Effective date

This act shall take effect on passage (Sec. 3).

Key definitions

  • Deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media: synthetic media that appears to a reasonable person to be a realistic representation of (A) a political candidate that injures the reputation of a political candidate; or (B) an individual that attempts to unduly influence the outcome of an election, including a public question, by providing materially false information to voters (§ 2031(1)).
  • Synthetic media: an image, an audio recording, or a video recording of an individual's appearance, speech, or conduct that has been created or intentionally manipulated with the use of digital technology, including artificial intelligence (§ 2031(2)).

Obligations

  • A person shall not, within 90 days before an election in Vermont, publish, communicate, or otherwise distribute synthetic media that the person knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media unless the person includes a disclosure stating: "This media has been manipulated or generated by digital technology and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur." (§ 2032(a))
  • For images and video recordings, the disclosure text must be easily readable by the average viewer and inclusive to the greatest extent possible of individuals with disabilities, and for video recordings, the disclosure must appear for the full duration (§ 2032(a)(1)).
  • For audio recordings only, the disclosure must be read in a clearly spoken manner and in a pitch and pace that can be easily heard by the average listener and inclusive to the greatest extent possible of individuals with disabilities, at the beginning, at the end, and if longer than two minutes, interspersed at intervals not greater than two minutes each (§ 2032(a)(2)).
  • A person upon whom a notice is served under civil investigation must comply with its terms unless otherwise ordered by a court (§ 2042(b)(1)).

Prohibitions

  • Publishing, communicating, or otherwise distributing synthetic media that the person knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media within 90 days before an election in Vermont without the required disclosure (§ 2032(a)).
  • Knowingly and intentionally violating any provision of this subchapter (§ 2033(a)).
  • With intent to avoid, evade, or prevent compliance with a civil investigation, removing, concealing, withholding, destroying, mutilating, altering, or falsifying documentary material (§ 2042(b)(2)).

Penalties and enforcement

A person that knowingly and intentionally violates a provision of this subchapter shall be fined not more than $1,000.00, unless the violation is with intent to cause violence or bodily harm (up to $5,000.00), or within five years after one or more prior violations (up to $10,000.00), or both (up to $15,000.00) (§ 2033(a)). A candidate whose appearance, speech, conduct, or environment is misrepresented may seek injunctive or other equitable relief prohibiting publication, communication, or distribution (§ 2033(b)). A State's Attorney or the Attorney General may institute any appropriate action, injunction, or other proceeding to prevent, restrain, correct, or abate any violation (§ 2041). The Attorney General or a State's Attorney may conduct civil investigations, including examining records, demanding written responses under oath, requiring attendance and testimony, and administering oaths (§ 2042(a)). Any person that fails to comply with a notice or destroys evidence with intent to avoid compliance shall be fined not more than $5,000.00 (§ 2042(b)(2)). Court enforcement of investigation orders; disobedience punished as contempt (§ 2042(c)(2)). Private right of action: candidate may seek injunctive or equitable relief (§ 2033(b)); no general private right of action for damages stated.

How it affects AI deployment

  • Organizations deploying AI to create or manipulate images, audio, or video of individuals must ensure that within 90 days before a Vermont election, any such synthetic media that they know is deceptive and fraudulent includes the required disclosure (§ 2032(a)).
  • The disclosure must meet specific format requirements for images, video, and audio, including accessibility considerations (§ 2032(a)(1)-(2)).
  • Organizations that are broadcasting stations, websites, streaming platforms, or mobile applications may be exempt if they meet certain conditions, such as bona fide news coverage with acknowledgment, being paid to broadcast, or federal law requirements (§ 2032(b)(1)).
  • Providers of telecommunications services, information services, or interactive computer services are exempt for content provided by another person (§ 2032(b)(4)-(5)).
  • Violations can lead to fines up to $15,000 depending on intent and prior violations, and candidates may seek injunctions (§ 2033).
  • Organizations may be subject to civil investigations by the Attorney General or State's Attorney, including demands for records and testimony (§ 2042).

Notable exemptions

  • Radio or television broadcasting stations, cable or satellite operators, programmers, producers, websites, streaming platforms, or mobile applications that broadcast deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media as part of bona fide newscast, news interview, news documentary, commentary of general interest, or on-the-spot coverage of bona fide news events, provided they clearly acknowledge questions about authenticity (§ 2032(b)(1)(A)).
  • Such entities when paid to broadcast deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media (§ 2032(b)(1)(B)).
  • Such entities when required by federal law to broadcast advertisements from legally qualified candidates (§ 2032(b)(1)(C)).
  • Websites or regularly published newspapers, magazines, or periodicals of general circulation that routinely carry news and commentary and clearly state that the media does not accurately represent the speech or conduct of the represented individual (§ 2032(b)(2)).
  • Persons that produce or distribute deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media constituting satire or parody (§ 2032(b)(3)).
  • Providers of telecommunications services or information services as defined in 47 U.S.C. § 153, for content provided by another person (§ 2032(b)(4)).
  • Providers of interactive computer services as defined in 47 U.S.C. § 230, for content provided by another person (§ 2032(b)(5)).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether any synthetic media you create or distribute falls within the definition of deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media under § 2031(1).
  • If distributing within 90 days before a Vermont election, ensure the media includes the exact disclosure statement: "This media has been manipulated or generated by digital technology and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur." (§ 2032(a)).
  • For images and video, format the disclosure text to be easily readable and inclusive of individuals with disabilities, and for video, keep it on screen for the full duration (§ 2032(a)(1)).
  • For audio, read the disclosure clearly at beginning, end, and at intervals not exceeding two minutes if longer than two minutes, with accessibility considerations (§ 2032(a)(2)).
  • Check if any exemption applies, such as bona fide news coverage with acknowledgment, satire or parody, or being a service provider for third-party content (§ 2032(b)).
  • Maintain records and be prepared to respond to civil investigation demands from the Attorney General or State's Attorney, including producing documents and testimony (§ 2042).
  • If a candidate, consider seeking injunctive relief if your appearance, speech, conduct, or environment is misrepresented (§ 2033(b)).

Sec. 1. 17 V.S.A. chapter 35, subchapter 4 is added to read:
 Subchapter 4. Use of Synthetic Media in Elections
§ 2031. DEFINITIONS
 As used in this subchapter:
 (1) “Deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media” means synthetic media
that appears to a reasonable person to be a realistic representation of:
 (A) a political candidate that injures the reputation of a political
candidate; or
 (B) an individual that attempts to unduly influence the outcome of an
election, including a public question, by providing materially false information
to voters.
 (2) “Synthetic media” means an image, an audio recording, or a video
recording of an individual’s appearance, speech, or conduct that has been
created or intentionally manipulated with the use of digital technology,
including artificial intelligence.
§ 2032. DISCLOSURE OF DECEPTIVE AND FRAUDULENT
 SYNTHETIC MEDIA
 (a) Disclosure. A person shall not, within 90 days before an election in
Vermont, publish, communicate, or otherwise distribute synthetic media that
the person knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media unless the person
includes a disclosure in the synthetic media stating: “This media has been
manipulated or generated by digital technology and depicts speech or conduct
that did not occur.”
 (1) For deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media consisting of images
and video recordings, the text of the disclosure shall appear in a size that is
easily readable by the average viewer and inclusive to the greatest extent
possible of individuals with disabilities. For video recordings, the disclosure
shall appear for the full duration of the video recording.
 (2) For deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media consisting of audio
recordings only, the disclosure shall be read in a clearly spoken manner and in
a pitch and pace that can be easily heard by the average listener and inclusive
to the greatest extent possible of individuals with disabilities, at the beginning
of the audio recording, at the end of the audio recording, and, if the audio is
 BILL AS INTRODUCED AND PASSED BY SENATE AND HOUSE S.23
2025 Page 14 of 17


greater than two minutes in length, interspersed within the audio recording at
intervals of not greater than two minutes each.
 (b) Exceptions. Subsection (a) of this section shall not apply to:
 (1) a radio or television broadcasting station, including a cable or
satellite television operator, programmer, or producer, or to a website,
streaming platform, or mobile application, that:
 (A) broadcasts deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media as part of a
bona fide newscast, news interview, news documentary, commentary of general
interest, or on-the-spot coverage of bona fide news events, provided the
broadcast clearly acknowledges through content or a disclosure, in a manner
that can be easily heard or read by the average listener or viewer, that there
are questions about the authenticity of the deceptive and fraudulent synthetic
media;
 (B) is paid to broadcast deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media; or
 (C) is required by federal law to broadcast advertisements from
legally qualified candidates;
 (2) a website or a regularly published newspaper, magazine, or other
periodical of general circulation, including an internet or electronic
publication, that routinely carries news and commentary of general interest,
and that publishes deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media, if the publication
clearly states that the deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media does not
accurately represent the speech or conduct of the represented individual;
 (3) a person that produces or distributes deceptive and fraudulent
synthetic media constituting satire or parody;
 (4) a provider of a telecommunications service or information service,
as those terms are defined in the Communications Act of 1934, 47 U.S.C. §
153, for content provided by another person; or
 (5) a provider of an interactive computer service, as defined in 47
U.S.C. § 230, for content provided by another person.
§ 2033. PENALTIES
 (a) A person that knowingly and intentionally violates a provision of this
subchapter shall be fined not more than $1,000.00, unless:
 (1) the person commits the violation with the intent to cause violence or
bodily harm, in which case the fine shall be not more than $5,000.00;

prior violations under this section, in which case the fine shall be not more
than $10,000.00; or
 (3) the person commits the violation with the intent to cause violence or
bodily harm and the person commits the violation within five years after one or
more prior violations under this section, in which case the fine shall be not
more than $15,000.00.
 (b) A candidate whose appearance, speech, conduct, or environment is
misrepresented through the use of deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media in
